objectives.text: ask “Are these your books?” and answer “Yes, they are.” while tidying up
name clothes: a jacket, pants, a shirt, a skirt, shoes and a sweater
use “What's that?” for one thing and “What are those?” for more than one
read School Clothes and compare what students wear to school in New Zealand, Brazil and France
hear the difference between the a and o sounds and read words with each
ask “How do I look?” and answer “It's too big.” or “You look great!”
describe clothes with opposites: big and small, long and short, old and new
describe clothes with “This skirt is short.” and “These pants are long.”
read People's Fashion, from Italy, and tell what people like to wear
hear the difference between the e and u sounds and read words with each
learn about traditional clothes that people wear in different countries
describe a traditional outfit using clothes words and colors
make a poster of the traditional clothes of one country
present their poster, naming the country and the clothes
ask “What's for lunch, Mom?” and answer “Tuna sandwiches.”
name lunch foods: chicken, fish, spaghetti, fried rice and salad
tell what others like and don't like: “She likes salad.” “They don't like salad.”
read It's Lunch Time! and compare school lunches in the USA and Japan
tell the h and j sounds apart in words they hear and read
say “Hurry up!” and “OK. I'm coming.” when it is time for art class
name art things: clay, glue, paint, a colored pencil, paper and tape
ask “Whose clay is this?” and answer with a name, like “It's Sam's clay.”
read Arts and Crafts, from the UK, and tell what people make
tell the s and z sounds apart in words they hear and read
learn the names of different art activities and the things each one needs
explain how to do an art activity step by step with first, next and last
make an art book with a page for each art activity
show a page of their art book and say what they used to make it
suggest “How about a board game?” and answer “That's a good idea.”
name things in a living room: a coffee table, a lamp, a rug and a sofa
tell what is in a room with “There is a TV.” and “There are lamps.”
read What's in the Living Room? and compare living rooms in Canada and Switzerland
tell the k and g sounds apart in words they hear and read
help a friend find something with “Look under your bed.” and “Oh, here it is.”
name bedroom things and place words: bookcase, computer, in, on, under and next to
ask “Where is the bag?” and answer “It's under the chair.”
read What's in the Room?, from Hong Kong, and tell where things are in the room
read and say words spelled with k and words spelled with qu

units.title: School Link 3 · Rooms in a house

objectives.text: learn the names of the rooms in a house and what people do in each
say what people do in a room, like “We sleep in the bedroom.”
make a house mobile with a piece for each room
tell the class about each room in their house mobile
ask “Do you like wild animals?” and answer “Yes, I do.” or “No, I don't.”
count from eleven to twenty and name a bear, a giraffe, a tiger and a zebra
ask “How many zebras are there?” and answer “There are four zebras.”
read Wild Animals of the World and tell which animals live in Australia, China, Indonesia and Argentina
tell the r and w sounds apart in words they hear and read
say “I'm sorry I'm late.” and answer “That's OK.”
name fun things: a bike, a camera, a kite, a skateboard and a soccer ball
ask “Does he have a kite?” and answer “Yes, he does.” or “No, he doesn't.”
read Favorite Things and tell what children in New Zealand, South Korea, Spain and France like
tell the w and y sounds apart in words they hear and read

units.title: School Link 4 · Counting numbers and ordinal numbers

objectives.text: learn the difference between counting numbers like one and two and order numbers like first and second
say who is first, second and third in a line
make a poster about order numbers like first, second and third
use their poster to tell the order of things, like “The cat is third.”
say “I'm bored.” and invite a friend with “Let's go out and play.”
name and act out dancing, jumping, running, sleeping and walking
ask “What's she doing?” and answer “She's walking.” or “They're walking.”
read Fun Things to Do and tell what people do outside in Vietnam, Canada, Belgium and Austria
hear and read words that start with ch, like chair, and with sh, like ship
ask a friend “What are you doing?” and then ask “Can I come over?”
name and act out drawing, painting, reading, talking and writing
ask “Is he talking?” and answer “Yes, he is.” or “No, he isn't.”
read Fun Hobbies and tell about hobbies in Argentina, Denmark, Spain and Peru
hear and read words that end with ch, like lunch, and with sh, like fish

units.title: School Link 5 · Different activities in gym class

objectives.text: learn the names of different gym class activities and how to do them
explain how to do one gym activity using action words
make a poster about their favorite gym class activity
tell why they like their favorite gym activity best
take turns in a game with “Can I go first?” and “Now, it's your turn.”
name activities: climb a tree, play the drum, play hopscotch and ride a bike
ask “Can they play soccer?” and answer “Yes, they can.” or “No, they can't.”
read School Talent Show, from the USA, and tell what the children can do
tell s and th apart at the start of words, like sink and think
ask “Can we get popcorn, Dad?” and answer “Yes, we can.” or “No, we can't.”
name snacks: chips, a cookie, a candy bar, popcorn and ice cream
ask “What does he want?” and answer “He wants ice cream.”
read Healthy Snacks, from Sweden, and tell which snacks are good for our bodies
tell s and th apart at the end of words, like bus and bath
learn the five food groups and name a food from each group
explain why we need food from every group to stay healthy
make a poster of a dinner plate with foods from the five food groups
tell the class what is on their plate and which group each food is in
